pages.title: Pre-write by prompt type
pages.note: Most schools reuse a handful of prompt types every year. Draft one strong version of each before secondaries arrive, then cut and adapt it per school. Word and character limits vary by school, so keep a long and a short version.

items: List 3 reasons you'd pick a school, beyond location
Write a reusable opening about what you want in training
Leave a slot for 2 school-specific details per school
Each detail ties back to something you've done
Pick one real difficulty, not a humblebrag
Keep the setup short; spend most words on what you did
End with what changed in how you work now
Check it doesn't repeat your personal statement
Brainstorm: background, identity, skills, experiences
Choose one specific story, not a list of traits
Say how it shapes the way you'd treat patients or peers
Write a 100-word and a 300-word version

sections.h: Gap year / what you're doing now
items: List current roles with start dates and hours
One line on why you chose each
Use present tense for anything still going
Note anything new since you submitted AMCAS
Decide if you need it: grade dip, gap, change of path
If yes, explain in plain words, no excuses
If not, a short update is fine, or leave it blank
Draft all five prompt types
Have one reader check them for clarity
Save every draft in one folder, one file per type
Look up each school's secondary fee and policy in MSAR
Set aside a budget for secondary fees
Log each secondary the day it arrives
Do schools with stated deadlines first
Aim for about 2 weeks per school, quality first
Goal: half done in the first 2 weeks, rest in the next 2
Have FAP? Ask schools that didn't waive the fee

items: Answer exactly the question they asked
Swap in this school's name and details everywhere
Search the draft for any other school's name
Under the word or character limit
Fee paid or waiver confirmed
Save a copy of what you sent for interview prep

pins.title: Med School Secondary Essays: 5 Prompt Types to Pre-Write
pins.description: Most med schools reuse the same few secondary prompt types every year: why us, a challenge, diversity, your gap year and an optional extra. How to pre-write each one before secondaries arrive, plus a free printable checklist.

pins.quote: Secondaries come fast once AMCAS reaches schools
pins.headline: Pre-write them in May
pins.title: When to Start Med School Secondary Essays (Before They Arrive)
pins.description: Secondaries show up soon after schools get your AMCAS application, often several in one week. Pre-write the common prompt types in May and June so each one only needs adapting. Free printable pre-writing plan.

pins.headline: Secondary essay pre-writing plan
pins.sub: Prompt-by-prompt checklist and a turnaround plan
pins.title: Free Printable: Med School Secondary Essay Pre-Writing Checklist
pins.description: A two-page printable for med school secondary essays: a checklist for each common prompt type, a plan for turning secondaries around, and a final check to run before you submit each one. Free PDF.

pins.headline: Applying to med school this cycle?
pins.sub: Draft your secondaries before they arrive. Here's how, prompt by prompt.
pins.title: Pre Med Tip: Pre-Write Your Secondary Essays
pins.description: Applying to medical school? Pre-writing your secondary essays is one of the best ways to keep up in July and August. A plan for each common prompt type and a free printable checklist from a current med student.

pins.headline: Before you hit submit on a secondary
pins.title: Med School Secondary Checklist: 6 Things to Check Before Submitting
pins.description: Before you submit a med school secondary: answer the exact question, swap in the right school's details, search for other schools' names, check the limit, confirm the fee or waiver, and save a copy for interview prep.

pins.description: See the reported secondary essay prompts for 150+ MD programs in one place, search by school or prompt type, and spot the ones that repeat across your list so you can pre-write once!
